cases.disposition_reason: TablePro with no --page flag opens Connections at 120×40 in truecolor with reduced motion. The landing lists Filter connections and Development and does not show Query 1. A click on Development shows host dev-db.internal.acme.io and database acme_dev. Connect finishes on Query 1 in catalog acme_prod › public, with status ✓ Connected to Development and the empty editor placeholder Type SQL. Loading schema, Query history, and Statement executed are absent. Ctrl+Q exits 0.
cases.entry_path: launch tablepro --color truecolor --motion reduced at 120x40 with no --page flag; click Development; click Connect
cases.return_path: the workbench is already Query 1; Ctrl+Q exits

cases.disposition_reason: On Query 1, Development Safe Mode stays Silent. The editor runs SELECT sku FROM products LIMIT 1. The finished grid is one row, the status is 1 row, the result tab is SELECT products (1), and the visible cell is SKU-01000. The editor is replaced with UPDATE products SET name = name WHERE sku = 't03-affected'. No Execute write query? dialog opens. The unpinned SELECT tab is gone. The body is a card titled Statement executed with Statement UPDATE products, Rows affected 2, and Duration 12 ms. The status line is ✓ UPDATE products · 2 rows affected · 12 ms. SKU-01000 and SELECT products are absent. The 120×40 frame is that card, with the statement on editor line 1 beside the Explorer. The 80×24 frame, captured before the terminal returns to 120×40, keeps the same statement, the UPDATE products (2) tab, the status line, and the card; the Explorer collapses to a rail. After both frames the card remains. Ctrl+Y opens Query history and lists t03-affected with 12 ms and 2 rows. Ctrl+W closes history and returns to Query 1 with the affected card still shown. Ctrl+Q opens Quit TablePro? because the editor is unsaved; confirming Quit exits 0.
cases.expected_results: The affected body shows the simulated count and History records that statement.
cases.forbidden_effects: The body shows rows from the previous SELECT.
